subject: Post-call: model fit & streaming quality next steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Choi <bryan@olivetx.com>; Sandra Lopez <s.lopez@olivetx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit & streaming quality next steps

Hi Bryan / Sandra —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good signal on the telehealth transcription + realtime summarization use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope an initial streaming evaluation: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: deliver sub-1s perceived latency for clinicians while streaming draft summaries and patient flags in near-real time.
- Volume profile: ~150 concurrent streams initially, spikes to ~500/day, median utterance lengths ~30–60 tokens, occasional long monologues (~400 tokens).
- Quality concerns: partial output coherence (mid-stream hallucinations), appropriate stop sequences for clinical notes, and avoiding truncated sentences mid-token.

Initial model-fit recommendations (high level)
- Candidate A: rw-text-1-large (quantized) — best cost/quality starting point for summarization workload.
- Candidate B: rw-stream-lite — tuned for chunked streaming; better incremental coherence but slightly higher cost.
- Fallback: rw-text-1-small for low-priority background jobs.

Attachments and links
- I uploaded a short prompt set you mentioned and a stub of our streaming benchmark: redwood_streaming_benchmarks_202602.pdf, prompt_set_v1.jsonl (attached).

Next steps proposed
1) Olive: send 24–48h sample transcripts and a few representative prompt templates (we can use the attached olive_sample_prompts.txt).
2) Redwood: run a 72-hour streaming eval on rw-stream-lite + rw-text-1-large (we'll record latency, chunk coherence, stop-sequence behavior).
3) Follow-up 30-min sync next week to review results and discuss pilot credits / procurement.

Open questions for the eval we want to confirm now:
- Target end-to-end latency SLO (perceived vs token latency) — you mentioned 800ms perceived earlier.
- Which stop sequences should we treat as authoritative for clinical notes (e.g., '\n
-- end note --' vs double-newline)?

I'll also loop in our solutions engineer Monica to capture technical settings for streaming chunking and stop sequences.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_streaming_benchmarks_202602.pdf]
[Attachment: prompt_set_v1.jsonl]
[Attachment: olive_sample_prompts.txt]

From: Bryan Choi <bryan@olivetx.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandra Lopez <s.lopez@olivetx.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & streaming quality next steps

Rishi — thanks for the recap and quick turnaround. This looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Perceived latency target: yes, 800ms for the clinician-facing UI is our target (95p). If you can measure both per-chunk latency and time-to-first-token that would be helpful.
- Stop sequence: our clinicians expect a clear note delimiter. Prefer double-newline followed by 'Assessment:' as the canonical signal, but we can provide a small list of acceptable terminators.
- We'll attach a small sample of live transcripts and our preferred prompt templates in a separate file (see attached: olive_sample_prompts.txt).

Also: we noticed the streaming output sometimes emits partial sentences mid-stream which causes UI artifacts. Curious how you plan to measure and detect mid-token truncation vs model hallucination.

Thanks — Bryan
VP Product, Olive Therapeutics
[Attachment: olive_sample_prompts.txt]

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Choi <bryan@olivetx.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit & streaming quality next steps — technical plan

Bryan / team — quick note from the solutions side with concrete config and how we'll evaluate the streaming UX issues you flagged.

Streaming behavior notes
- Chunking: we'll stream in 64-token chunks with overlap=8 tokens to preserve context across boundaries; empirically this reduces sentence splits.
- Stop sequences: treat double-newline + 'Assessment:' as a hard stop token sequence. We'll add post-processing to hold the final chunk until a full sentence boundary is observed (simple punctuation heuristic) to avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
- Latency measurement: we will emit metric timelines for time-to-first-byte and per-chunk token latency; we'll compute 95p perceived latency using your UI render timing traces if you provide them.

Model suggestions and evals
- rw-stream-lite (recommended for the initial streaming eval): streaming-optimized attentions, maintains incremental coherence.
- rw-text-1-large (quantized): run as a comparison for final summary pass (non-streaming).
- We will run both in our sandbox and produce: token-level perplexity, ROUGE-L on your reference summaries (where available), and a streaming-coherence score (internal metric that flags sentence fragments and hallucinated entity insertions).

Regression detection
- We'll run continuous eval across the 72-hour trial and will alert on quality regressions vs your baseline prompt set using the provided prompt_set_v1.jsonl. Alerts will be via Slack and we will annotate failing prompts with the exact token timestamps that diverged.

Attachments and artifacts
- I uploaded our internal streaming benchmark summary (redwood_streaming_benchmarks_202602.pdf) and an eval plan spreadsheet (streaming_eval_plan.xlsx).

Next steps summary
1) Olive: confirm the list of acceptable stop sequences and drop the UI trace file (time series) into the shared Drive.
2) Rishi/Redwood: kick off the 72-hour streaming eval once we have the sample transcripts (we'll notify when results are available).

I'll set the eval defaults: chunk_size=64, overlap=8, stream_timeout=250ms; we can tweak after the first run.

- Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_streaming_benchmarks_202602.pdf]

Monica — this is super helpful, thanks. A couple quick asks before you start the run: 
- Can you include a variant with chunk_size=32 and overlap=4 so we can see the tradeoff (latency vs coherence)?
- Pricing/credits: what's our likely bill for a 72-hour eval on rw-stream-lite at the volumes we discussed? We want to surface this to procurement.

I'll upload the UI trace file today and confirm the stop sequence set.

Best,
Bryan
